core_obligations: Show that a family alpha of r-cycles on fibres of X/S with S locally Noetherian and f locally of finite type is a relative r-cycle if and only if every flat pullback f_i^*alpha along a jointly surjective family of flat morphisms f_i : X_i to X locally of finite type of relative dimension e is (proof lines 1032-1058). Forward direction: lemma-relative-cycle-functoriality (tag 0H51) (proof lines 1033-1034). Converse: let g : S' to S be a morphism from the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring; replacing S by S', X by its base change and alpha by g^*alpha reduces to the case S a valuation ring with closed point 0 and generic point eta, where one must show sp_{X/S}(alpha_eta) = alpha_0 (proof lines 1035-1039); denote f_{i,0} and f_{i,eta} the base changes of f_i to the two points; then f_{i,0}^* sp_{X/S}(alpha_eta) = sp_{X_i/S}(f_{i,eta}^* alpha_eta) by lemma-specialization-flat-pullback (tag 0H4L), and the latter equals f_{i,0}^* alpha_0 because f_i^*alpha is a relative cycle by assumption (proof lines 1047-1053); since the family of pullback maps f_{i,0}^* : Z_r(X_0) to Z_r(X_{i,0}) is jointly injective (the f_{i,0} are jointly surjective and flat, so a nonzero prime cycle component would survive flat pullback over its generic points, which are all hit), sp_{X/S}(alpha_eta) and alpha_0 have equal pullbacks under all f_{i,0}^* and hence are equal (proof lines 1054-1057).
proof_roadmap: Forward direction by functoriality of the relative cycle property (proof lines 1033-1034).
Reduce the converse to testing against valuation rings (proof lines 1035-1039).
Pull the desired specialization identity back to each member over the closed point: first equality by flat-pullback compatibility of specializations, second by assumption (proof lines 1047-1053).
Conclude by joint injectivity of the closed-fibre pullback maps, from joint surjectivity and flatness (proof lines 1054-1057).
